by: the automation kernel's gates on convention strength, fallback preservation, performance and validation before persistence
check.population: every static list, switch or registry the automation pass considers
check.freshness: a verdict stands until the code or its conventions change
check.refusal: the kernel refuses to automate a candidate whose convention, fallback or validation contract fails
check.observation: the discovery and startup reports dynamic loading must emit, which locate an extension that failed to load
check.evidence: none: the catalog states this check as a class, so a watched run belongs to each system that adopts it
check.authority: the discovered convention, which replaces the static list and which the startup report is compared against

records.title: Static-to-Dynamic Readiness

exemplar.before: A static list rewritten as dynamic discovery on sight, adding fragility for no gain.
exemplar.after: static pattern → classify intentional vs problematic → maintainability pressure + convention strength → {automate | retain static | formalize convention first}

records.intent: Detect static implementation patterns, classify whether they are intentional or problematic, measure maintainability pressure, verify convention strength, and automate only when stability or fallback exists.
records.invariant: Static code is not debt by default; automation requires evidence that dynamism reduces maintenance risk without increasing fragility.

records.title: Runtime-Neutral Automation Boundary

exemplar.before: Automation logic hardcodes a runtime's glob and path, so it runs on one platform only.
exemplar.after: semantic op{DISCOVER/READ/SEARCH/VALIDATE/PERSIST} → adapter maps to the runtime → portable core, no platform mechanics inside

records.intent: Express discovery, reading, searching, validation, persistence, and reporting as semantic operations, then delegate concrete mechanics to runtime adapters.
records.invariant: Dynamic architecture must be portable across runtimes by separating automation intent from platform execution.

records.title: Automation Operation Mode

exemplar.before: Analysis silently mutates source; a design run also implements.
exemplar.after: detect mode{analysis | design | implementation | validation} → bind permissions → mutation only in implementation mode → mode-legal artifact

records.intent: Detect operation mode, bind allowed actions, prohibit source mutation outside implementation mode, and emit analysis, design, implementation, or validation artifacts accordingly.
records.invariant: Automation design and automation execution are separate contracts.

records.title: Capability Degradation

exemplar.before: Automation assumes it can execute and persist, then fails silently when it can't.
exemplar.after: required capabilities → probe → {full | degraded | blocked} → execute | emulate | skip-with-disclosure | block

records.intent: Declare required capabilities, probe availability, emulate missing behavior where safe, disclose unavailable capability, and downgrade confidence or block dependent operations.
records.invariant: Automation systems must not silently assume filesystem, execution, persistence, validation, or search capabilities.

records.title: Automation Opportunity Detection

exemplar.before: Automation targets guessed instead of found from repeated manual coordination points.
exemplar.after: scope → detect{manual registration, hardcoded reference, static list, duplicated discovery} → classify{location, type, count, maintenance signal}

records.intent: Search target scope for manual registries, hardcoded references, static lists, and duplicated discovery logic; then classify each finding with count, location, role, and maintenance signal.
records.invariant: Automation candidates emerge from repeated manual coordination points.

records.title: Intentional Static Separation

exemplar.before: A small, stable, bounded static list flagged as debt and automated away.
exemplar.after: static finding → scale + change-frequency + risk → {intentionally-static candidate | automation candidate | needs more evidence}

records.intent: For each static pattern, compare size, frequency, stability, and risk; classify small or stable patterns as intentionally static candidates instead of automation debt.
records.invariant: Keeping a static list may be correct when the domain is bounded and explicitness improves safety.

records.title: Breaking Point Calculation

exemplar.before: Automation prioritized by aesthetic preference, not scale pressure.
exemplar.after: current count + growth rate + limits{cognitive, maintenance, duplication} → time until breach → severity

records.intent: Measure current item count, estimate growth rate, compare against cognitive and maintenance limits, compute time or units until threshold breach, and assign severity.
records.invariant: Automation priority should be driven by scale pressure, not aesthetic preference.

records.title: Automation Priority Ordering

exemplar.before: Migrations tackled in arbitrary order, low-impact first.
exemplar.after: breaking points → urgency{severity + time-to-break + scope + maintenance cost} → sorted backlog

records.intent: Convert breaking points into urgency scores using severity, projected time-to-break, affected scope, and expected maintenance cost, then sort candidate migrations.
records.invariant: Automation work should be sequenced by operational impact.

records.title: Convention Strength Analysis

exemplar.before: Auto-discovery built on a naming convention only 60% of files follow.
exemplar.after: related resources → naming tokens + organization → consistency % → {strong → auto-ready | moderate → formalize | weak → establish convention first}

records.intent: Discover related resources, extract naming tokens and organization patterns, calculate consistency percentages, and mark auto-discovery readiness only when convention strength passes threshold.
records.invariant: Convention-based discovery is safe only when conventions are measurable.

records.title: Extension Interface Discovery

exemplar.before: Dynamic discovery attempted with no contract boundary to validate against.
exemplar.after: implementations → contract signals{inheritance, composition, common methods, common schema} → interface candidate when count exceeds threshold

records.intent: Search for inheritance, composition, shared method contracts, and shared schema contracts; group similar implementations; infer interface candidates when implementation count exceeds threshold.
records.invariant: Dynamic discovery requires an explicit or inferable contract boundary.

records.title: Scalability Projection

exemplar.before: Automation judged against today's 5 items, not tomorrow's 500.
exemplar.after: current scale → 10x + 100x projection → manual feasibility → {manual ok | dynamic recommended | dynamic required}

records.intent: Measure current resource counts, project tenfold and hundredfold growth, assess manual maintenance feasibility, and identify where dynamic discovery becomes necessary.
records.invariant: Automation architecture should be evaluated against future scale, not only current scale.

records.title: Performance-Aware Discovery Design

exemplar.before: Dynamic discovery ships, hiding a per-startup scan cost that grows with scale.
exemplar.after: item count → {discovery cost, loading cost, memory} vs targets → cache only when justified → failure modes recorded

records.intent: Estimate discovery and loading cost, compare large-scale cost against performance targets, introduce caching only when justified, and record failure modes.
records.invariant: Dynamic discovery must not hide runtime performance debt.

records.title: Dynamic Extension Architecture

exemplar.before: Implementations loaded dynamically with no contract validation, unobservable.
exemplar.after: contract → discovery → contract-validate → {load valid | skip invalid | manual override | isolate failure} → report{discovered, manual, skipped, failed}

records.intent: Infer extension contracts, define discovery conventions, validate discovered implementations against the contract, preserve manual registration fallback, and report discovered, skipped, failed, and manual items.
records.invariant: Dynamic loading must be contract-validated and observable.

records.title: Centralized Reference Resolver

exemplar.before: The same hardcoded path duplicated at a dozen call sites.
exemplar.after: reference group → resolver → scope-safe rule → config override fallback → map each old reference to the resolver

records.intent: Group duplicated hardcoded references, derive resolver names, define scope-safe resolution rules, provide configuration override fallback, and map each old reference to a resolver migration.
records.invariant: Hardcoded resource access should be centralized only through validated resolution boundaries.

records.title: Cache Invalidation Strategy

exemplar.before: Discovery results cached with no invalidation, serving stale data forever.
exemplar.after: cache subject → key{scope, convention, adapter version, identity} → invalidate on{resource change, explicit, time, implementation change}

records.intent: Define cache keys by scope, convention, adapter version, and implementation identity; invalidate by resource change, explicit request, time expiry, or implementation version change.
records.invariant: Caching dynamic discovery is safe only when invalidation semantics are explicit.

records.title: Manual Fallback Preservation

exemplar.before: Auto-discovery removes the escape hatch — a non-conforming item can't be registered.
exemplar.after: auto-discovery + manual registration for exceptions → deterministic merge → manual items reported separately

records.intent: Keep explicit registration paths for non-conforming or exceptional implementations, order manual entries deterministically, and report manual items separately from auto-discovered items.
records.invariant: Automation should reduce manual maintenance, not remove escape hatches.

records.title: Dynamic Failure Isolation

exemplar.before: One bad extension crashes the whole dynamic system.
exemplar.after: item failure{discovery | loading | validation} → isolate the item → continue with valid ones → report the failure; halt only if systemic or critical

records.intent: On individual discovery, loading, or validation failure, isolate the failing item, continue with valid items where safe, and report the failed item with reason.
records.invariant: One bad extension must not collapse the whole dynamic system unless marked critical.

records.title: Entry Point Migration

exemplar.before: Discovery registries built but the composition root still hardcodes registrations.
exemplar.after: composition roots → scan static patterns → update to discovery + resolver → validate → persist only in implementation mode

records.intent: Locate composition roots, identify manual registrations and hardcoded references, compose updates that use discovery registries and centralized resolvers, and apply only in implementation mode.
records.invariant: Dynamic architecture takes effect at composition boundaries.

records.title: Measured-vs-Estimated Validation

exemplar.before: An estimated performance number reported as if it were measured.
exemplar.after: validation need → can measure? → {measured | estimated (labeled)} → estimated is never reported as measured

records.intent: Run validation when execution is available; otherwise estimate from static evidence, label the result as estimated, and never report estimated performance as measured.
records.invariant: Validation truthfulness requires provenance on every metric.

records.title: Architecture Validation Before Persistence

exemplar.before: A generated resolver saved before it is checked against the architecture rules.
exemplar.after: generated artifact → schema check → architecture check → {persist | reject | emit unpersisted}

records.intent: Validate generated contracts, registries, resolvers, plans, and entry point updates against schemas and architectural rules before saving or modifying any artifact.
records.invariant: Generated architecture must satisfy structure before it becomes state.

records.title: Knowledge Capture

exemplar.before: Each automation session forgets the last — the same analysis re-run.
exemplar.after: knowledge base + session findings → merge{detections, conventions, scale, designs, migration, validation} → persist when capability exists

records.intent: Load or initialize the automation knowledge base, merge new detections, conventions, scalability concerns, architecture designs, migration history, and validation outcomes, then persist when capability exists.
records.invariant: Automation systems improve when each session updates durable architectural memory.

records.title: Automation Session Report

exemplar.before: A report that conflates the design intent with what was applied.
exemplar.after: session → {detection, convention, scale, architecture, implementation, measured-vs-estimated validation, limitations} → report separating design from applied

records.intent: Summarize detected patterns, convention readiness, scalability pressure, dynamic architecture, generated artifacts, implementation status, measured versus estimated validation, and limitations.
records.invariant: Automation reports must separate design intent from applied implementation and disclose degraded capability.

records.title: Automation Completion Status

exemplar.before: 'Automated' declared while the convention was never formalized, no fallback was preserved, and the validation was estimated not measured.
exemplar.after: convention strong + fallback preserved + performance validated + architecture validated + capability disclosed → complete; else planned_only | blocked

records.intent: Mark the static-to-dynamic automation complete only when convention strength passed, a manual fallback is preserved, performance and architecture validation passed with measured provenance, and any degraded capability is disclosed; otherwise report planned-only or blocked.
records.invariant: Automation completion is a verified terminal state — never a claim while convention, fallback, validation, or capability evidence is absent.

records.title: Automation Kernel

exemplar.before: A static pattern rewritten dynamic by intuition, with no convention, fallback, or validation.
exemplar.after: init → capabilities → detect → classify → conventions → scale → design → optional implement → validate → knowledge → report

records.intent: Load configuration, verify capabilities, initialize knowledge, detect static patterns, classify automation opportunity, analyze conventions, assess scale and performance, design dynamic architecture, optionally implement, validate, update knowledge, and report.
records.invariant: Static-to-dynamic refactoring is a gated evidence pipeline that only automates when convention, fallback, performance, and validation contracts are satisfied.

records.title: <Automation Concern>
records.intent: <Detect static coordination point> → <Classify intentional vs problematic> → <Measure scale pressure> → <Verify convention strength> → <Design dynamic contract> → <Preserve fallback> → <Validate performance and architecture> → <Capture knowledge>
records.invariant: Any static implementation should become dynamic only when the domain has stable conventions, bounded failure modes, observable discovery, and safe manual fallback.
